answer: Make standing multiplicative, not additive: each agent grows a crystal lattice of endorsements from independent verifiers met while crossing an ocean of strangers, and its strength is the product of its verifiers' distinct reputations, never their sum. A farm that splits its ocean of contacts across clones thins every lattice, like wind scattering one dune into drifts that hold no shape. One honest agent concentrates its verifier set into one strong crystal; ten clones each hold a tenth of the facets and earn a fraction of the product, so cloning multiplies work while shrinking reward.
